concepts.title: Nutrients and Balanced Diet
concepts.definition: Food supplies six classes of nutrients -- carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals and water -- each with its own work in the body. A balanced diet combines them in right amounts for one's age and activity, using food groups, so that energy, repair and protection are all met without excess.
concepts.key_idea: Six nutrients, five food groups, one aim -- a plate balanced for your age and work.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehe103.txt nutrient sections (carbohydrates proteins fats vitamins minerals water, balanced diet, food groups, RDA mention)

solution_steps.explain: Energy nutrients are carbohydrates and fats; body-building is protein; protection comes from vitamins, minerals and water.
Foods fall into functional groups -- energy-giving, body-building, protective -- that simplify meal planning.
Combine the groups in amounts suited to age, sex and activity to reach a balanced diet.

concepts.title: Nutritional Needs of Adolescents and Meal Planning
concepts.definition: The adolescent growth spurt raises demands for energy, protein, calcium and iron; girls additionally need iron against menstrual losses. Meal planning for this stage favours frequent, nutrient-dense meals, breakfast never skipped, and moderation in sugary, fried and processed snacks.
concepts.key_idea: Feed the growth spurt -- calcium for bones, iron for blood, breakfast for the brain.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehe103.txt adolescent sections (growth spurt demands, calcium iron needs, meal planning, snacking habits, importance of breakfast)

solution_steps.explain: Match meals to the spurt: more energy, more protein for muscle, calcium for bone, iron for expanding blood volume.
Three meals plus planned snacks keep energy steady; breakfast anchors concentration through school.
Keep fried, sugary and highly processed items occasional, not habitual.

concepts.title: Health, Fitness and Hygiene Practices
concepts.definition: Health is more than absence of disease -- a state of physical, mental and social well-being. Fitness grows from regular exercise, adequate sleep and hygiene habits; food safety in storage and preparation protects the health that nutrition builds.
concepts.key_idea: Nutrition builds, exercise trains, hygiene protects -- the three legs of everyday health.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehe103.txt health sections (definition of health, physical fitness, exercise, hygiene, food safety and storage)

solution_steps.explain: Take health as complete well-being -- body, mind and social relations -- not merely no illness.
Regular activity builds endurance, strength and flexibility, complementing diet.
Personal and food hygiene -- washing, safe storage, clean preparation -- keep infection from undoing nutrition.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Classify these foods into their nutrient groups: rice, dal, ghee, papaya, spinach, water.

solution_template.explain: Rice is carbohydrate; ghee is fat -- both energy-giving.
Dal supplies protein for growth and repair.
Papaya (vitamin A/C), spinach (iron, vitamins) and water complete the protective balance.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A 16-year-old girl skips breakfast and feels dull by mid-morning. Diagnose and correct using the chapter.

solution_template.explain: A skipped breakfast after a long overnight fast starves the brain of glucose during the growth-spurt years.
A nutrient-dense breakfast -- sprouts or egg, milk, fruit, whole grain -- restores energy and iron and calcium intake.
A mid-morning snack such as fruit or nuts prevents the next slump.
